key_insight: In metal-halide perovskites, localized carrier spin relaxation is dominated by hyperfine coupling to nuclear spins, with holes generally relaxing via metal nuclei and electrons via halogen nuclei, so exact dynamics matter more than simple exponential fits.
engineering_relevance: Understanding which ions set spin lifetime can guide perovskite composition choices that improve carrier spin stability and enable better opto-spintronic characterization.
method: Adapted a muon-spin relaxation model to carrier spins
Solved longitudinal spin relaxation exactly across arbitrary hyperfine correlation times
Applied the model to time-resolved Faraday rotation on two perovskite samples
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that fitting experimental time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two samples extracts microscopic parameters such as localization volume and hyperfine correlation time, and shows mono-exponential fits are inadequate in the intermediate regime.
watch_item: The model is focused on localized carriers and hyperfine-driven relaxation, so its conclusions may not directly transfer to delocalized carriers or samples where other spin-relaxation channels dominate.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
